item.title: MongoDB Setup
item.description: This walkthrough uses MongoDB 7.0.16 as a single-node replica set with a persistent Docker volume. PMS writes policies and ADS follows the same database through a change stream. The example listens on loopback without authentication for local development. Production authentication, TLS and replica set configuration follow the walkthrough. MongoDB must run as a replica set or sharded cluster. ADS watches the database with a change stream, and replacing the whole policy store runs in a transaction; a standalone mongod supports neither.

item.title: Pluggable Storage
item.description: Built-in stores and extension contracts The standalone binaries register file, etcd, MongoDB and MySQL implementations under pkg/store. Availability does not mean identical operational guarantees; review backend authentication, persistence, transaction and watch behavior for your deployment. The configuration below illustrates property names; running etcd/MongoDB deployments is outside this local example. A full backend implements pms.PolicyStoreManager: service, authorization-policy, role-policy and function management, snapshot reads and watch/stop. ADS accepts the narrower PolicyStoreManagerADS read/watch interface.

item.title: etcd Setup
item.description: This walkthrough uses an external etcd v3.6.14 server with a persistent Docker volume. PMS writes policies and ADS watches the same key prefix. The single-node example listens on loopback and uses plain HTTP for local development. Production TLS and cluster configuration follow the walkthrough. 1.
